chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from an-Nadr and Safwan from Ibn Sinan from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
He said: 'Do not trim your hair while you intend Hajj in Dhi al-Qa'dah, nor in the month in which you intend to depart for Umrah.'

key_terms.تَأْخُذْ مِنْ شَعْرِكَ: Trim/take from your hair (referring to cutting hair or removing body hair)
key_terms.ذِي اَلْقَعْدَةِ: Dhi al-Qa'dah (the 11th month of the Islamic calendar)

ai.seo_question: When should a Muslim stop trimming their hair before performing Hajj or Umrah?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* specifies the timing for preserving one's hair (keeping the *Hillu*) as a prerequisite for the validity of Hajj and Umrah, linking the ritual state to the specific months of Dhi al-Qa'dah and the month of departure. It underscores the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on the physical manifestation of the *Ihram* state beginning well before the actual entry into the sacred boundaries, ensuring the pilgrim is ritually prepared from the outset of the designated period.
